messages.text: I’ll inspect the specification and executable interface, then build focused pytest cases and a runner that writes JUnit XML reliably.

The specification defines a large multicall interface, with especially precise contracts for help, parser diagnostics, and several text-file workflows. I’m building reusable fixture helpers and keeping tests isolated so a single failure won’t prevent the rest of the suite from running.

The suite now covers shared CLI behavior across every listed command, plus focused text-fixture tests for help diagnostics, coordinate transforms, replication, XVG statistics, and XPM rendering. I’ve also checked the test files compile; the workspace does not include the program-under-test binary, so behavioral runs will happen in the evaluation workspace.

Created the pytest suite under `/workspace/eval`. It covers shared help and parser behavior for the documented commands, with focused tests for text-based workflows.

`run.sh` is executable and runs the full suite with JUnit output at `/workspace/eval/results.xml`. The tests compile successfully; I couldn’t run them against the program because `/workspace/executable` isn’t present in this authoring workspace.
I’ll inspect the program specification first, then build focused pytest cases and a runner that always writes JUnit results.

Created the pytest suite in `/workspace/eval`, with focused tests for search behavior, options, filtering, output modes, configuration, and generated completions. The normative type and completion files are copied into `eval`, so tests do not depend on authoring-only files.

`/workspace/eval/run.sh` is executable and runs the full suite with JUnit output at `/workspace/eval/results.xml`. I checked that the test file compiles; I did not run the suite because `/workspace/executable` is not present.
I’ll inspect the specification in the workspace, then build focused tests and an executable runner that produces JUnit XML even when tests fail.

Created the suite in [test_cli.py](/workspace/eval/test_cli.py) and an executable [run.sh](/workspace/eval/run.sh). The focused tests cover the documented CLI modes, validation, file and stdout routing, configuration behavior, and diagnostics. The runner invokes pytest from `/workspace/eval` and writes JUnit XML to `/workspace/eval/results.xml`, including when individual tests fail.

I did not run the suite.
